Print and standard methods for causal results

print.lcc_result.Rd

print() shows the estimator, the variables, the estimates with standard errors, confidence intervals and p-values, and overlap diagnostics. coef() and nobs() return the estimates and the number of rows used.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
print(x, digits = 3, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
print(x, digits = 3, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

x, object

A result of intervene_membership() or intervene_effect().

digits

Number of decimal places.

conf.level

Confidence level of the printed intervals.

Value

print(): x, invisibly. coef(): a named numeric vector (lcc_result: \(\Delta_k\) by class; intervention_result: psi1, psi0, effect). nobs(): an integer.

Details

Output uses UTF-8 symbols (\(\Delta\), \(\psi\), superscripts) when the locale supports them; set options(latentclasscausal.ascii = TRUE) for ASCII output. The intervention printout warns about near-violations of positivity (smallest post-intervention profile probability below 0.01).

See also

tidy.lcc_result(), causal_table()

Examples

data(programme)
# \donttest{
# print, coef and nobs for the effect of the school programme
# measurement model of the eight follow-up wellbeing items only (no treatment, no covariates)
m <- latentmixtures::lca(programme, low_mood:friends, K = 3)   # Flourishing, Moderate, Distressed
#> Starting Julia ...
r <- intervene_membership(m, programme, treatment = programme,
                confounders = c(female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging))
print(r, digits = 2, conf.level = 0.90)
#> ▸ Causal effect of a treatment on latent class membership
#>   AIPW, BCH pseudo-outcomes, 5-fold cross-fitting; N = 2000, K = 3
#>   Treatment:    programme
#>   Confounders:  female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging
#> 
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            P(C¹=k)  P(C⁰=k)      Δ    SE          90% CI      p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class 1     0.63     0.43   0.20  0.03    [0.15, 0.25]  <.001
#>   Class 2     0.24     0.29  −0.06  0.04   [−0.12, 0.00]   .129
#>   Class 3     0.14     0.28  −0.14  0.02  [−0.18, −0.11]  <.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>   Δ = P(C¹=k) − P(C⁰=k); SE from the influence function incl. the measurement model.
#>   Diagnostics: entropy = 0.666, propensity range [0.019, 0.923]
coef(r)   # Delta for each class: positive for Flourishing, negative for Distressed
#>     Class 1     Class 2     Class 3 
#>  0.19623314 -0.05540049 -0.14083265 
nobs(r)
#> [1] 2000
# }
